W3.rationale: Level 1 anchor: work-situated learning exists as an optional internship. The program describes WIL as an opportunity, and the two internship courses sit as two of four alternatives in the capstone list for accounting and finance majors, so no core unit necessarily places a student in a workplace — the level-2 requirement of a core unit with practitioner supervision and assessment is not met. The alternative marketing-major capstone is a planning project with no course page in the extract, so no workplace setting, supervision or host accountability is documented. This cohort is not documented as already practising, so the in-practice route does not apply.

G1.rationale: PASS condition: a coherent specialist core with progressive technical depth — an accredited sequence and an all-compulsory specialist core. Every major lists an all-compulsory course set that runs level I to level III within the discipline (introductory accounting through corporate accounting and auditing; business finance through portfolio theory and topics in corporate finance), and the program is built for professional accreditation with CPA Australia, CA ANZ, the CFA Institute and the AMI. This is not generic or interchangeable content.
evidenceLines: The Bachelor of Commerce is designed to prepare students for professional accreditation in accounting, finance or marketing. Students completing an accounting major will be entitled to join the CPA Australia (Certified Practising Accountants) and CA ANZ (Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand); the finance major meets the entrance requirements of the CFA Institute (Chartered Financial Analyst); and the marketing major is accredited with the AMI (Australian Marketing Institute).

A capstone is a qualification requirement for every major, with live-project and internship options.
